SSD vs. HDD: what’s the difference?

Tech Compass · Updated 2026-10-19

IN THIS GUIDE

The quick answerWhat you notice in daily useCapacity and compatibilityNeither is a backupFurther reading
THE QUICK ANSWER

An SSD stores data in flash memory. An HDD stores it on spinning magnetic platters. Both keep files without power, but SSDs usually access data much faster.

What you notice in daily use

An SSD usually reduces the wait when starting a computer, opening apps, or loading files. It does not automatically speed up every calculation or solve an internet connection problem.

Capacity and compatibility

Choose a drive that fits the device’s interface and physical space. M.2 describes a form factor; it does not by itself guarantee which storage protocol is supported. Consult the device manual before buying.

Neither is a backup

Either type can fail. Keep a separate copy of important files and check that you can restore them. Before replacing a system drive, plan how you will transfer your files and reinstall or migrate the operating system.

What is RAM?

RAM is your computer’s short-term working memory. It holds the information your apps are using right now. Storage keeps your files when the power is off; RAM does not.

Why is my computer running slowly?

A slow computer may be short of memory or storage space, busy with background work, or getting too hot. Start by finding what is busy instead of installing a cleaner app.
